newsitem.title: USA: W.R. Grace likely to spin off temp staffing unit.
newsitem.headline: W.R. Grace likely to spin off temp staffing unit.

text.p: W.R. Grace & Co. is likely to sell or spin off Cross Country Staffing, a division that provides temporary health care workers, to the public next year, the head of the unit said Tuesday.
"We have no delusion we are part of Grace's long-term strategy," Cross Country Chief Executive Joseph Boshart said during a meeting with reporters.

Packaging and speciality chemicals group Grace owns just over 60 percent of Cross Country, in partnership with Nestor-BNA Plc of Britain, and has been selling and spinning off businesses in an ongoing restructuring. Grace last year rejected a merger offer from Hercules.
"I would anticipate that sometime in 1998 there will be liquidation," Boshart said, unless a downturn in the U.S. stock market or a recession upsets that timetable.

Other staffing companies such as industry giant Olsten might be strategic buyers of Cross Country, which places nurses for short-term assignments and other temporary health workers to hospitals across the nation, Boshart said.
But Cross Country has had no contact with any potential buyers, he said. "We would prefer to remain independent."
Boshart said Cross Country, with annual revenues of $124 million, dominates its sector in the temporary health worker business, and is now looking for growth outside its core businesses.
Cross Country is starting an information-technology unit to supply software engineers, programmers and other computer specialists to health care organisations needing temporary help.

Jonathan Ward, head of the new unit, said health care organisations spend about $1 billion a year on information technology workers and that Cross Country hoped to have $5 million of that business by year end.
Grace's stock rose 50 cents to $54.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
